items.a: Gantt chart of insulin time profiles: rapid lispro acts from 15 minutes, peaks at 1 hour and lasts 3 to 4 hours; regular acts from 30 minutes, peaks at 2 to 3 hours and lasts 6 to 8 hours; cloudy NPH peaks between 4 and 10 hours and lasts 10 to 16 hours; glargine is flat with no peak and lasts about 24 hours.

items.t: Receptors and pharmacodynamics: the core ideas
items.c: Log dose-response: competitive antagonist shifts curve right (higher EC50, same Emax); non-competitive depresses Emax.
items.a: Sigmoid log concentration-response curves showing a full agonist at Emax 100 percent, a competitive antagonist causing a parallel rightward shift with preserved Emax, a non-competitive antagonist depressing Emax to 50 percent, and a partial agonist reaching submaximal efficacy.
items.rn: Receptors and pharmacodynamics: the core ideas

items.c: Elimination kinetics: first-order rate is concentration-dependent (constant half-life); zero-order rate is constant and saturable.
items.a: Comparative plasma concentration decline curves over time: first-order elimination shows exponential decline with constant half-life (constant fraction eliminated per hour); zero-order elimination displays linear decline (constant amount eliminated per hour).
items.rn: Distribution and pharmacokinetic parameters

items.c: Therapeutic index: ratio of toxic dose (TD50) to effective dose (ED50); narrow margins require therapeutic drug monitoring.
items.a: Therapeutic index curves plotting cumulative population frequency against drug dose: effective dose curve (ED50) and toxic dose curve (TD50). The therapeutic index is the ratio TD50 to ED50, defining the margin of safety.
items.rn: Distribution and pharmacokinetic parameters
